answer: One concrete defense is bonding every agent identity to a slashable stake and a slow reputation ledger. To register, an agent locks real tokens; its score then grows only through paid, verifiable work. A sybil farm cannot cheaply mass-produce identities, because each fake agent needs its own locked capital and must survive a periodic audit pulse before earning trust. Attacking with a thousand hollow accounts means a thousand deposits at risk, and one fraudulent claim burns them all. The entry price moves from a free email to locked copper, so the attack stops paying.
